description: Ask the user one to four multiple-choice questions and wait for the answers. Use it only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you can't settle from the request, the code or a sensible default, such as choosing between approaches or settling an ambiguous requirement. Don't use it for facts you can find out yourself, to ask permission or whether to proceed, or for choices with a conventional default: take the obvious one, say so and go on. Ask everything you need in one call, as the last call of your reply: calls after it in the same reply are not run. The user may see only your questions, not the text before the call, so each must stand alone: give the facts needed to answer it and never refer to "above". Give each question two to four distinct options; put the one you recommend first and end its label with "(Recommended)". The user can always type their own answer, so never add an "Other" option. Read the answers carefully and follow what they actually say; if the user skipped a question, decide yourself and say what you assumed.

header.description: A short tag shown above the question, at most 12 characters, such as "Database".

multi_select.description: Let the user choose more than one option. Defaults to false.

description.description: What choosing this means, in one sentence.

label.description: The choice, in one to five words.

question.description: The whole question, ending with a question mark.

name: ask_user
